NOTE: The following instructions assume that you first scan the patient and then press Freeze .
Press Measure once; an active caliper displays.
To position the active caliper at the start point (distance) or the most anterior point (tissue depth), move the Trackball.
To fix the start point, press Enter. The system fixes the first caliper and displays a second active caliper.
To position the second active caliper at the end point (distance) or the most posterior point (tissue depth), move the Trackball.
To complete the measurement, press Enter. The system displays the distance or tissue depth value in the measurement results window.
Press Measure once; an active caliper displays.
To position the active caliper, move the Trackball.
To fix the start point, press Enter. The system fixes the first caliper and displays a second active caliper.
To position the second caliper, move the Trackball.
Adjust the Ellipse; an ellipse with an initial circle shape appears
To position the ellipse and to size the measured axes (move the calipers), move the Trackball.
To increase the size, rotate the Ellipse button clockwise. To decrease the size, contrarotate the Ellipse button
To complete the measurement, press Enter. The system displays the circumference and area in the measurement results window.

Measurement/Calculation worksheets are available to display and edit measurements and calculations. There are generic worksheets as well as Application specific worksheets. The worksheets are selected from the Measurement Touch Panel.
NOTE: Probes can be connected at any time, whether the unit is ON or OFF
Place the probe's carrying case on a stable surface and open the case.
Carefully remove the probe and unwrap the probe cable.
DO NOT allow the probe head to hang free. Impact to the probe head could result in irreparable damage.
Align the connector with the probe port and carefully push into place.
Carefully position the probe cord so it is free to move and is not resting on the floor.
The probe activates in the currently-selected operating mode. The probe's default settings for the mode and selected exam are used automatically.
Gently wipe the excess gel from the face of the probe. (Refer to the Basic User Manual for complete probe cleaning instructions).
Carefully slide the probe around the right side of the keyboard, toward the probe holder. Ensure that the probe is placed gently in the probe holder.
4-40 LOGIQ e – Basic Service Manual 5937432-1EN Rev. 4
Probes can be disconnected at any time. However, the probe should not be selected as the active probe.
Pull the probe and connector straight out of the probe port.
Carefully slide the probe and connector away from the probe port and around the right side of the keyboard.
Be sure that the probe head is clean before placing the probe in its storage box.
Take the following precautions with the probe cables: Do not bend. If you have purchased the cart option, be sure to keep probe cables free from the wheels.
Be careful not to trip on the probe cables if using the device without the optional cart.

A cineloop is a sequence of images recorded over a certain time frame. When using ECG the time frame can be adjusted to cover one or more heart cycles. When frozen, the System automatically displays the cineloop boundary markers on either side of the last detected heart cycle.
Press Freeze, then roll the Trackball to activate CINE. To start CINE Loop playback, press Run/Stop. To stop CINE Loop playback. press Run/Stop.
Press First to move to the first CINE frame; press Last to move to the last CINE frame.

Press the Start Frame Two-Button Softkey to move to the beginning of the CINE Loop. Adjust the Start Frame up/down Two-Button Softkey upward to move forward through the CINE Loop. Adjust the Softkey downward to move backward through the CINE Loop.

Press the End Frame Two-Button Softkey to move to the end of the CINE Loop. Adjust the End Frame up/down Two-Button Softkey upward to move forward through the CINE Loop. Adjust the Softkey downward to move backward through the CINE Loop.
Adjusting the CINE Loop Playback Speed
Adjust the Loop Speed up/down Two-Button Softkey to increase/decrease the CINE Loop playback speed.
Moving through a CINE Loop Frame By Frame
Adjust the Frame by Frame up/down Two-Button Softkey to move through CINE memory one frame at a time.

LOGIQ e – Basic Service Manual 4-43 5937432-1EN Rev. 4
Backup and Restore Database, Preset Configurations and Images
To Format the backup media, DVD:
Go to Utility -> Connectivity -> Removable Media.
Select the media type from the drop down menu.
Enter the label for the media. It is best to use all capital letters with no spaces or punctuation marks. Press Format.
A pop-up message displays to inform operation completed. Press OK .
If desired, verify that the format was successful by selecting Verify in Utility -> Connectivity -> Removable Media. see Figure 4-17 on page 4-44 .
4-44 LOGIQ e – Basic Service Manual 5937432-1EN Rev. 4

NOTE: Always backup any preset configurations before a software reload. This ensures that if the presets need to be reloaded, after the software update, they will be the same ones the customer was using prior to service.
Insert a formatted DVD-R disk into the drive.
Go to Utility -> System -> Backup/Restore NOTE: If you are not logged in as GE Service or with administrator privileges, the Operator Login window is displayed. Log on with administrator privileges.
In the Backup list, select Patient Archive , Report Archive and User Defined Configuration and Service .
In the Media field, select DVD(or USB memory device) .
The system performs the backup. As it proceeds, status information is displayed on the Backup/Restore screen.
For the User defined configurations, please refer to Detail Restore of User Defined .

4-52 LOGIQ e – Basic Service Manual 5937432-1EN Rev. 4
One button backup and restore allows you to perform backup and restore of the user defined configuration to the local hard drive as described in this section.
Before performing one button backup function, make sure to disconnect the probe from the system and restart.
After system restarted and entered the scanning page, press Ctrl + B to backup user defined configuration.
After backup is done, a message will display on the screen as " Backup completed".
Before performing one button restore function, make sure to disconnect the probe from the system and restart.
After system restarted and entered the scanning page, press Ctrl + R to restore user defined configuration.
After restore is done, system will be restarted automatically.

1 | Power on the system. | 
2 | Connect USB memory stick with USB port on the system. | 'New hardware device detector' icon display on the status bar.
3 | Click the 'New hardware device detector' icon | Check whether the device driver installed successfully.

Step | Task | Expected result(s)
1 | Power on the system. | 
2 | Connect Barcode Scanner via the USB port on the system. | A beep should be heard.

semantic_nodes.canonical_text: NOTE: If any one of the two Pass or Fail criteria listed below are met, the result is a failure.
Total number of element failures exceeded;
Number of adjacent element failures exceeded (based on a pre-defined gap between elements which are considered adjacent).

Probe Check is a probe assessment tool that evaluates each probe element response scanning in the air. Probes have to be clean, any gel residue will provide incorrect data. This test is an assessment that is intended to be used comparatively during the life of the probe to evaluate possible probe deterioration over time.
Probe Check can detect most probe defects, but not all possible probe defects.
GE is NOT responsible for the confirmation about the normal function of the ultrasound probe before use.
Probe check will evaluate the probe performance and provide the user with an indication of potential impact to the diagnostic image if it is compromised due to transducer malfunction.
Probe Check supports on 4C-RS, E8C-RS, 3Sc-RS,6S-RS, 8C-RS, 12L-RS, L8-18i-RS, 9L-RS, C1-5-RS, L4-12t-RS, L10-22-RS, 6Tc-RS, ML6-15-RS, L4-20t-RS, 12S-RS,M5Sc-RS, LK760-RS probes.
Probe Check provides five interval options for auto triggering, press Utility -> System -> General -> Probe Check to select the preset.
Never: probe check will never automatically open.
Every time: probe check will automatically open and check probes each time they are activated.
Once a day: probe check will automatically open and only check the probe the first time it is activated each day.
Once every 7 days: probe check will automatically open once every week and check the probe the first time it is activated that week.
Once every 30 days: probe check will automatically open once a month and only check the probe the first time it is activated that month.
NOTE: The system default is every time for USA region. For other regions, the system default is Never. The first boot up shall follow this setting.
User shall perform probe check manually if the auto trigger interval is not configured as "every time" when changing a probe with the same name as previous probe.
NOTE: When Probe Check is not set as Never, it will be triggered automatically while switching the probes, switching the presets individually will not trigger Probe Check.
4-70 LOGIQ e – Basic Service Manual 5937432-1EN Rev. 4
DO NOT allow the probe head to hang free. Impact to the probe head could result in irreparable damage.
Do NOT unplug the probe during Probe Check process, otherwise the test result shall be failed.
NOTE: Always remember to clean the probe surface before probe check procedure.

Check that the probe to be tested is thoroughly clean and dry. For cleaning the probe, refer to See 'Care and Maintenance' on page 10-1 for more information. Connect it to the probe port on the scanner, then hold the probe in the air ready for testing.
NOTE: The auto trigger assessment is only available when the Probe Check preset is Every Time.
NOTE: The auto trigger assessment is only available for the probe connected to the activated probe port.
NOTE: Prior to inserting the probe, ensure that the connector locking handle is positioned to the unlock state.
NOTE: Ensure the probe is locked to the system before you start the probe diagnostics.
Press Probe, select the probe then the system will do probe test automatically, a message will pop-up on the monitor "Probe Check:Testing probe, please wait...".
If the probe test is Passed, there will be a message "Probe Check: Probe test passed." showing on the monitor.
4-72 LOGIQ e – Basic Service Manual 5937432-1EN Rev. 4
If the probe test is Failed, the checking results will be shown on the pop-up window.

NOTE: The testing results may vary in different series of GE ultrasound products due to differentiated design. If you have any concern with the testing result, please contact with your service partner.

Follow the suggestions shown on the pop-up window to contact with your service partner, follow the guidance from your service partner to determine if there is issue with the probe or the system itself.
A manual probe check should be conducted when images acquired with a deficient probe look abnormaly. Phenomenon includes but not limited to overall decreased brightness or/and partial signal loss.
Figure 4-44. Normal image acquired with L6-12-RS
Examples (phantom scanning) are provided below for your reference. Whenever you see similar cases or aren't confident in the status of a probe, please perform probe check manually.
Condition 1: Total number of element failures exceeded.
Figure 4-45. Abnormal image acquired with a deficient L6-12-RS probe that has distributed defect elements
4-74 LOGIQ e – Basic Service Manual 5937432-1EN Rev. 4
Condition 2: Number of adjacent element failures exceeded.
Figure 4-46. Abnormal image acquired with a deficient L6-12-RS probe that has adjacent defect elements
Users can perform probe check manually:
Press Exam, select the probe to be tested, click Test Probe button.
Click Test Probe button on the pop-up window. The testing workflow is same as Auto Trigger from step 2 to step 5, refer to 'Auto Trigger' on page 4-72 for information.
4-76 LOGIQ e – Basic Service Manual 5937432-1EN Rev. 4
